body: Let's add a test to ensure that this is communicated to be intended behavior and catch any possible errors going forward

> Having to jump through the hoops for `StringLikeVariantOrder`, when that should probably just be the default. Obviously outside the scope of this PR, which just makes the sorting work as it intuitively should

This is a matter of performance, most of the time we don't care about the lexicographical order of `StringName`, only that it's a stable order (in a session), comparing `StringName` by pointer is significantly faster than doing it by `String` comparison (`O(1)` for the former, `O(n)` for the latter), so sorting by string comparison should generally be opt-in for `StringName`

Note that for `Array` we should update the documentation as it is now incorrect, it says:
> The final order is dependent on the "less than" (<) comparison between elements.

Which is not true now, so this is a part of documented API which makes it far trickier to change

I'd say to split this into two PRs, one for `Dictionary` and one for `Array`, as `Dictionary` sorting is newer and the specific method of sorting is undocumented

I don't think the compatibility breakage for `Array` is critical as the previous behavior (other than that `StringName` and `String` were sorted by type) is not usable as `StringName` ordering is essentially random AFAIK, but it still breaks the fact that `StringName` and `String` are now merged, previously all `StringName`s were grouped and all `String`s were grouped, which *is* something you could rely on

> Note that for `Array` we should update the documentation as it is now incorrect, it says:
> 
> > The final order is dependent on the "less than" (<) comparison between elements.
> 
> Which is not true now, so this is a part of documented API which makes it far trickier to change

How has this changed? Why would sorting no longer be strictly dependent on this comparison? Is it just a special case for **String** & **StringName** to make note of?

It has changed as I described it, previously `StringName` were sorted by themselves, and `String` by themselves, now they are together, and additionally `StringName`s are sorted by actual lexicographical order as opposed to pointer order, which is less critical:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a210fe6dbd27cc01bffacb0ce2816e0cf303af5e/core/variant/variant.cpp#L879-L887

~But the `<` operator for `Variant` compares first by type, then by value, so `StringName` is sorted entirely by themselves, and `String` by themselves, also "just a special case" is very much not the same~ Edit, this is not really the part used, and comparison is random currently

As far as I see it, taken from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105073 , this is all that could be said for `sort()`'s description.
> Sorts the dictionary in ascending order, by key. The final order is dependent on the "less than" ([code]<[/code]) comparison between keys. [StringName] keys are sorted as if they were [String].

I do have to agree that this is a more notable issue in **Dictionary** than **Array** and that perhaps the PR should be split.
Perhaps it's no severe issue at all, though, and we're all just crossing our bridges before we're coming across them. <sub><sub>Well, not me, because I did casually come across it, but you get the idea.</sub></sub>

The `Array` sorting is a bit more broken in some ways, in its current form, so this does fix issues, and it fails randomly at times because of the fact that the current comparison fails to order different types (at random)

But at least the documentation should be clarified, especially since the current description is partially unhelpful, as you can't actually use the comparison operator like this in GDScript

So the current behavior is technically actually not using the plain `Variant::operator<` but just the evaluation, which returns `false` for mixed types, making the result random

But I think a separate PR to discuss the specifics would be good

See:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/58878
Perhaps an alternative solution to this PR would be to implement "greater than" and "less than" operations between **String** & **StringName**?

Not to sound like a broken record, but this is another area where C++20 would benefit us. The three-way comparison operator & a `concept` for an equivalent "compare" evaluator would help us unify this logic so that we no longer have to juggle edge-cases.

I'd say the two options here are:
* Fix the basic comparison to handle types correctly, using `Variant::operator<`, which is likely what `Array::sort` was *meant* to do
* Use `StringLikeVariantOrder`, which changes behavior in some cases, but the baseline behavior is broken so doesn't change much

But I think this needs more discussion and evaluation, so splitting into two distinct PRs would be a good first step IMO to evaluate the two somewhat different situations (as `Array::sort` is *much* older)

The less-than operator for Variant can't be used so long as it sorts by type before value *exclusively*. That is: a lower-value `float` should never be sorted above a higher-value `int`, but it would with the current less-than implementation

The real problem is that we simply don't have universally-defined comparison logic. We have countless comparison handlers and individualized sorting schemes, but we shouldn't necessarily always be relying on that for how *containers* sort their contents. This wouldn't *need* C++20 to happen, but that would give us a convenient framework to devise such a system

We had a core meeting about this a few weeks back.
We found that we don't really have much consistency with sorting in the first place, but changing sorting will probably break _someone's_ project. We can still attempt minor fixes, but 'big consistency' changes probably have to wait for 5.0.
Closing this PR since it's unlikely it can be merged at any point, at least in this form.
